newsitem.title: GEORGIA: Georgian rebel region declares state of emergency.
newsitem.headline: Georgian rebel region declares state of emergency.

text.p: Georgia's breakaway region of South Ossetia has reimposed a state of emergency to deal with a crime wave, government officials in the region said on Tuesday.
An official in charge of the state of emergency said it included a midnight to 5 a.m. curfew in the regional capital Tskhinvali.
"The state of emergency has been imposed because of the crime situation in South Ossetia," Tskhinvali commandant Rustam Yuskayev told Reuters by telephone.
Yuskayev said the state of emergency would last for two months. He said it had been in place for several years until July, when it automatically lapsed.
He said acts of banditry such as theft of crops and property had increased since and so the separatist government had decided to reimpose it.

Georgian and South Ossetian irregulars clashed in 1991-92 after the region, mostly populated by ethnic Ossetians, declared independence in response to what they said was growing nationalism in Georgia after the break-up of the Soviet Union.
The fighting killed 1,000 and left more than 10,000 refugees. The conflict is one of several which bedevilled Georgia and led to its partial dismemberment following independence.
Peace talks since have made only limited progress at resolving the political status of the region, formerly home to 98,000 people.
No state has recognised South Ossetia. The region has fallen on hard times economically and has recently been riven by a wave of lawlessness.
